title: DeepSeek V2: absorbed MLA (one latent row per layer) with fine-grained MoE

installs.name: dsv2lite-16b
installs.note: 64 experts top-6, MLA, 27 layers; measured 2026-10-29 (the family's first lab A/B)

recommended.why: the deepseek2 flow is deliberately sequential; --chunk off is the only driver

the 2026-10-29 sweep read s64 +28.05% and s32 +11.09% decode over 16 slots (3/3 clean pairs each); the cost is peak: 15.65 GiB at 64 against 4.15 at 16 on a 15.5 GiB model, so 64 needs a large-memory host, 32 is the mid point, 16 the tight-memory choice

sweeps.description: expert cache slots at streamed residency

findings.workload: tslab sweep slots: protocol medium-review, 64 decode, chunk off, streamed residency; 3 clean pairs per candidate, 0 dirty in the sweep's verdict pairs
findings.conditions: the verdict field is s64's (sweep best); s32's WIN is verdict 1793275027265-2823-50; sweep record 1793275027275-2823-52; bit_exact; null floor 0.00% under the 2% default (record 1793273465426-20288-24); the candidates' memory growth (+3.83 and +11.50 GiB) exceeds the 64 MiB allowance by design - the expert cache is the mechanism; the s64 peak nearly equals the 15.5 GiB model, i.e. nearly all experts resident
findings.note: the family's first lab A/B: decode is expert-cache-bound on this MLA MoE and scales monotonically with slots; 64 is the throughput default on large-memory hosts, 32 the mid point (+11.1% for +3.8 GiB), 16 the tight-memory choice

open_questions: no install measured by the lab yet
MLA attention has no kernel bench; its latent projections come from the resident index
traps: the attn_decode bench refuses MLA layers; the int4_matmul bench carries the kv_a and kv_b latent shapes instead
